results.title: Inside a five-year-old startup’s rapid AI makeover
results.content:
Balint added the concept of “Sources” to the Craft Terminal: the ability to add other data sources – APIs, databases, MCP servers – on top of Craft Docs. The customer service team then started creating automations for common support tasks like sending discounts to emails on academic domains. The implementation of using APIs for sources is pretty clever: an API source acts like an MCP server to the agent, but Craft Agents hijacks the request and adds the credentials needed without the agent having access to those sensitive credentials.

However, the terminal interface was not beloved by Craft’s users. On December 18, he shared the Craft Terminal Agent with 15-20 external beta users. Feedback was positive and they liked it, but there were complaints about the terminal environment: [...] > “Zendesk wanted to charge us $20,000 per year for an AI integration that – to me – did not feel powerful at all. Frankly, this was one reason I started to build Craft Terminal, and then Craft Agents: I figured we can do a lot better than this.
>
> All our customer support flows now run through Craft Agents. We only use Zendesk as a backend.
>
> I want us to move to an API-first customer support solution. It feels to me that Zendesk is a really complex UI, one that is really slow, has bad API hooks, and just keeps breaking our flow.
> [...] The Craft team is in phase one: everyone is using the most capable models and finding out how the models boost their work. There will be time later to think about how to change workflows. Part of changing workflows comes pretty naturally by making changes to Craft Agents.

### Devs’ struggles

Several engineers are struggling with the sudden change and there have been resignations, as a result. One engineer quit shortly after Balint’s AI mandate, who was one of Craft’s early engineers and one of the very few devs who knew the codebase inside out.

results.title: Agent Craft — One voice note. Every channel covered.
results.content: Post that, and you reach a professional audience that can directly advance your career. But you have to say something you might regret. I've watched plenty of execs freeze at that edge. The second camp wins, and it isn't close. When I launched Agent Craft, my sixth company, I told the real version: I built around an assumption that didn't survive first contact with prospects, realised the value wasn't in an individual product but in a team one, then pivoted, rebranded from Influence Craft, and relaunched. That's not a "thrilled to announce" post. That's the human experience of working through a hard problem, which is exactly what LinkedIn is missing. If you've posted the hard version, the one with the sharp edges left on, I want to know whether it paid off or bit you. [...] It took about 15 minutes to process. I went and grabbed a coffee. When I came back it handed me its findings, all verified against its data. I tried reviewing a feature with Claude Science, and it changed how I'll approach the next one. Claude Science is Anthropic's science-backed platform. I'd stumbled across it a while back, downloaded it, and finally had a reason to use it. Here's the reason. I was reviewing a feature and wanted to check whether the angle I'd picked held up against actual patterns, not just my own hunch. So I gave it the data points I was working with and asked it to sort what the evidence supported from what it didn't, then work out the algorithm from the facts that survived. I used it on a small feature and it paid off. What I keep coming back to is that you don't [...] Almost nobody using AI right now is doing it correctly, and it has nothing to do with the tools. Your AI problem isn't really about AI. It's about the data you never collected. The tools don't fall short. There's just nothing solid to feed them. I watch CEOs ask the same question over and over. What should I do with AI today? How do I integrate it? Where are the cost efficiencies, the profitability efficiencies? All reasonable. All the wrong question. For most small businesses to really use AI, the question is different. What can I do today to prepare me to use AI profitably in the future? Here's why that matters. AI is not human intelligence. It looks at patterns and data, finds the anomalies, and predicts. The current LLMs and transformer-based models everyone's excited about need data
